_comment: Highest counts this repository is allowed to carry, and the critical/high advisory ids it carries per target. Lower both by fixing advisories and re-running `node scripts/audit-ratchet.mjs --update`; raising a count or adding an id is a deliberate edit that belongs in a commit message with a reason. A new advisory that cannot be fixed yet goes in `accepted` as { id } or { package, range } with a reason and an expires date (YYYY-MM-DD).

server.why: the API — every request goes through it

agent-hub.why: the SPA served to every user

desktop.why: runs on the user's own machine, outside any sandbox we control

..why: root dev tooling — dev:all, build scripts

accepted.reason: No fixed release exists (3.0.3 is the latest). braces is reached only through http-proxy-middleware -> micromatch (server, nextcloud-connector) and nodemon (dev). The advisory needs attacker-controlled glob PATTERNS; none of our createProxyMiddleware calls (server/routes/webpagesFullTierProxy.js, nextcloud-connector/src/proxy.js, ncProxy.js) passes a pathFilter, so micromatch never expands a pattern, let alone one from a request. Revisit when braces publishes a fix.
accepted.reachability: Reviewed all production createProxyMiddleware calls in server/routes/webpagesFullTierProxy.js, nextcloud-connector/src/proxy.js and nextcloud-connector/src/ncProxy.js against http-proxy-middleware 4.2.0 and micromatch 4.0.8. None configures a glob pathFilter; no user-controlled pattern reaches braces. Proxy HTTP/WebSocket regression suites cover these call sites. Nodemon is development-only.
